issues.display_title: Issue #1750: [Editor] Settings tab labels render dark on dark background
issues.main_description_html:
Description

In the Settings tab of the editor, most labels in the Gallery Adjustments and Advanced Settings sections render in a dark/near-black color on the dark panel background. Contrast is so low the labels are barely readable.

Same defect class as the artwork (#1747), object (#1748) and text (#1749) detail panels.

Affected text

Element Location
Floor Color / Wall Color general.component.html:95 (.adjusment__label)
Light Intensity Gallery general.component.html:106
Light Intensity 3D-Objects general.component.html:134
Camera Height general.component.html:163
Autoplay Speech Description general.component.html:199
Camera Speed general.component.html:221
Camera Rotation Speed general.component.html:248
Donut Size general.component.html:275

Gallery Adjustments, Advanced Settings and Hide Donuts render in a readable light gray, so the styling is inconsistent within the same panel.

Note: Advanced Settings is readable only because it binds its color explicitly at general.component.html:213 ([style.color]="… ? '#e7e7e7' : '#979797'"). Every neighbouring <span> that does not set a color is the one rendering dark — this points directly at a missing default color rather than a per-label mistake.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Open the editor of any virtual gallery
  2. Go to the Settings tab
  3. Toggle on Advanced Settings to reveal the lower section
  4. Look at the labels listed above

Expected

All labels in the Settings tab use the same light foreground color as the rest of the editor sidebar and meet the WCAG AA contrast ratio (4.5:1) against the dark panel background.

Actual

The listed labels render dark on dark, effectively invisible without straining.

Notes

Shared editor styles live in _editor.scss (.content-slide .title-content). Labels that define no text color inherit a dark default instead of the sidebar's $color-gray3. A single fix at that level should cover the Artworks, Objects, Text and Settings panels together (#1747, #1748, #1749).

Environment

  • Page: Editor → Settings
  • Branch: development

issues.display_title: Issue #1752: [Editor] Edit Frame dialog labels render low-contrast on dark background
issues.main_description_html:
Description

In the Edit Frame dialog (Artworks → artwork → Edit Frame), most control labels render in a low-contrast muted blue-gray on the dark dialog background instead of the readable light gray used elsewhere. The labels are hard to read across all four tabs (Canvas, Passepartout, Frame, Saved).

Same defect class as the editor panels reported in #1747, #1748, #1749, #1750 and #1751.

Affected text

All in edit-frame.component.html:

Tab Element Location
Canvas Thickness line 105
Canvas Color line 129
Passepartout Texture line 161
Passepartout Thickness line 218
Passepartout Width line 246
Passepartout Passepartout Measurements line 281
Passepartout Round Corners line 368
Passepartout Color line 401
Frame Thickness line 475
Frame Width line 503
Frame Frame Measurements line 538
Frame Round Corners line 625
Saved No data / Loading ... line 726

Readable by comparison: the dialog title Edit Frame, the tab names, Texture and Color in the Frame tab (rendered via <label> at line 425 and line 650), Save This Frame and Apply to all Artworks. So the same word (Texture, Color) is readable in one tab and low-contrast in another purely depending on whether it is marked up as <label> or <span>.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Open the editor of any virtual gallery
  2. Go to the Artworks tab and select an artwork
  3. Open Edit Frame
  4. Walk through the Canvas / Passepartout / Frame / Saved tabs and look at the control labels

Expected

All labels in the dialog use the sidebar's light foreground color ($color-gray3 / #E7E7E7) and meet the WCAG AA contrast ratio (4.5:1) against the dark dialog background.

Actual

The labels listed above render in a muted low-contrast blue-gray, noticeably dimmer than the surrounding readable text.

Notes

edit-frame.component.scss styles <label> and button text explicitly but leaves the bare <span> labels without a color, so they fall back to an inherited value. Aligning the <span> labels with the existing <label> styling should fix the whole dialog in one change.

issues.display_title: Issue #1758: [Editor] Show a notice on video artworks instead of playing them
issues.main_description_html:
Context

Follow-up to #1756. That change removed the video upload option, so no new video artwork can be added. But galleries created earlier still contain video artworks, and those kept playing normally in the editor.

That is confusing: the video plays, so it looks supported, while the feature behind it is not.

What changed

Video artworks no longer play. The artwork canvas now shows a plain notice instead:

Video artwork is not available at the moment.

This applies to every video artwork, not only broken ones. Everything else about them stays the same — they keep their frame, passepartout, position and size, and can still be selected, moved and deleted.

One side effect worth noting: opening a gallery is a little faster. The editor used to call an external service once per video artwork to resolve its stream. That is gone, and with it a failure case that could leave the editor stuck on the loading screen.

Files touched:

  • src/app/shared/services/artwork-loader.service.ts
  • src/app/pages/virtual-gallery/editor/editor.component.ts
  • src/assets/img/video-unavailable.png (new)

Note on the earlier approach

An earlier attempt showed this message as a hover tooltip instead of on the artwork itself. It was dropped in favour of putting the notice directly on the artwork, so it is visible without the user having to discover it.

Worth recording for whoever picks up video support later: the BabylonJS build used by the editor is not the same one the gallery uses. The editor build is missing pieces the gallery relies on for hover effects, so hover behaviour cannot simply be copied between the two projects.

Remaining / follow-up

  • Video upload code is now fully unused (AddVideoComponent and the video helpers in ImagesService). Decide whether to delete it or keep it for a future revival.
  • Align the BabylonJS builds used by villume-admin and villume-gallery so behaviour can be shared.

Verification

Build, type check, lint and formatting all pass. Still needs a manual check: open a gallery that contains a video artwork and confirm the notice shows up in place of the video.

issues.display_title: Issue #1766: Move Send Feedback from the side menu to the header, open in a new tab
issues.main_description_html:
Problem

Send Feedback sits in the dashboard side menu, where it is easy to miss. Clicking it also navigates the current page away to the contact form — in the editor that means losing the gallery you were working on just to report something about it.

What changes

Move the button to the header. Send Feedback becomes an icon button in the top-right of the header, directly to the left of the theme toggle, styled the same as the theme toggle. Hovering it shows a "Send Feedback" tooltip.

Remove it from the side menu.

Show it only where it belongs. The button appears only for signed-in users on dashboard pages. On the landing page it is hidden, signed in or not.

Open the contact form in a new tab. Clicking Send Feedback opens the contact form in a new tab instead of leaving the current page. The form arrives pre-filled exactly as it does today — subject "Beta Feedback" and a note about the page the feedback came from.

The editor keeps its own Send Feedback button in the editor toolbar, unchanged in position, and it also opens in a new tab now. The gallery you are editing stays open behind it.

Done when

  • Feedback button is in the header, left of the theme toggle, same look, with a "Send Feedback" tooltip
  • Feedback entry is gone from the side menu
  • Button visible on dashboard pages when signed in; hidden on landing
  • Clicking it opens a new tab with the contact form pre-filled

issues.display_title: Issue #1768: [Editor] Polish the Add New button and sidebar tab bar
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Tidy up two controls at the top of the editor sidebar: the "Add New" button that starts every panel, and the tab bar above it.

Add New button

The button sits at the top of Artworks, Objects, and Text. It kept its familiar look — full width, dashed outline, label with a plus on the right — but a few things were off:

  • It ran flush against both edges of the sidebar. It now sits inset with a little breathing room above it.
  • Its label and plus icon were nudged into place by hand rather than simply centred, so they could drift.
  • Pressing it gave no feedback, and a disabled button looked much the same as an active one.
  • The focus outline appeared on ordinary mouse clicks, not just keyboard navigation.

Tab bar

Artworks, Objects, Text, Settings, and Publish.

  • Hovering an inactive tab only changed the text colour, which was easy to miss in a dense panel. Inactive tabs now get a background tint on hover.
  • Hovering the active tab turned its label dark against its coloured fill. It now keeps its light label.
  • Tabs now respond visibly when pressed.
  • Tabs were built as links even though they don't navigate anywhere. They are now buttons, and each one announces whether it is the current tab, so screen readers and keyboard users get the right behaviour.

Also

The "Set Animation Sequence" row under the Artworks button had uneven spacing; its padding now lines up with the button above it.

Not included

  • No change to what any of these controls do.
  • No backend, API, or data model changes.

Checks

  • Add New works in Artworks, Objects, and Text, including the "Creating text…" state.
  • All five tabs still switch panels.
  • Tabs reachable and operable by keyboard, with a visible focus ring.
  • Active tab label stays legible on hover.

issues.display_title: Issue #1769: [Editor] Match the media support upload row to the Add New button and title field
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Bring the "media support" row under an artwork — the control that attaches a video or audio file to Artwork Info — in line with the rest of the editor sidebar.

Upload control

Before a file is attached, the row showed a link-styled label inside a dashed box: primary colour, underlined on hover, nothing like the other panel actions.

  • It is now the same control as the "Add New" button at the top of each panel — full width, dashed outline, muted label, same height, hover and disabled states included.
  • It is a real button instead of a link, so keyboard and screen-reader behaviour matches the other panel actions.
  • A long label truncates with an ellipsis instead of spilling out of the box.

Attached-file row

Once a file is attached, the row shows its name plus edit and delete icons.

  • The row keeps the same box as the Add New button, so both states line up.
  • The name field is now styled like the exhibition title field at the top of the sidebar: transparent, tinted on hover, focus ring on keyboard focus, ellipsis when the name is long.
  • Edit and delete icons became evenly sized square hit areas with a hover tint, instead of hand-tuned margins.

Not included

  • No change to upload, rename, or delete behaviour — same handlers, same conditions.
  • No backend, API, or data model changes.

Checks

The current Redux store contains unused main and user slices plus editor fields that only receive writes. Keeping them makes the state architecture harder to understand before the editor is migrated to Angular Signals.

  • Remove the UPDATE_INFO_USER and UPDATE_USER_STORY dispatches from the layout user-loading flow.

  • Preserve the Redux root shape as { editor } so existing redux-watch('editor.*') paths remain compatible.

issues.display_title: Issue #1772: [Editor] Introduce EditorSessionStore with Angular Signals
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Introduce a feature-focused Angular Signals store for serializable editor session state. This creates the target state boundary before active Redux notifications are migrated.

Scope

  • Add an injectable EditorSessionStore for editor UI and domain state that belongs to Angular.
  • Keep writable signals private and expose readonly signals and computed state.
  • Define typed editor state for active tab, selection identity, saving/blocking flags, and serializable session metadata needed by later migration issues.
  • Provide explicit mutation methods instead of exposing writable signals.
  • Keep Babylon.js objects such as Engine, Scene, meshes, materials, gizmos, and vectors outside the store.
  • Add focused unit tests for initial state, mutations, readonly exposure, and computed state.

  • Removing Redux dependencies.

issues.display_title: Issue #1774: [Editor] Replace Redux editor notifications with Angular Signals
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Replace Redux timestamp/event-bus notifications for object updates and undo/redo refreshes with Angular Signals.

Scope

  • Replace updateObjectData and undoRedo Redux fields with explicit Signals-based change notifications.
  • Migrate every remaining redux-watch subscription to signal-aware consumption.
  • Remove manual Redux unsubscribe bookkeeping made obsolete by Angular signal lifecycle handling.
  • Preserve component refresh behavior after transform changes, selection restoration, and undo/redo.
  • Prefer meaningful counters or typed event payloads over Date.now() timestamps.
  • Remove migrated Redux actions and reducer fields after the final consumer is converted.

Out of scope

  • Reworking the undo/redo snapshot algorithm.
  • Moving Babylon.js objects into Signals.
  • Removing Redux packages until no consumer remains.

Acceptance criteria

  • Object detail controls refresh after Babylon transform/data updates.
  • General, Publish, Objects, Artwork, and Text controls refresh after undo/redo.
  • No redux-watch imports or store.subscribe calls remain in editor components.
  • No updateObjectData or undoRedo Redux state remains.
